name: Beef Nihari
description: Slow-cooked Pakistani beef stew with deep spices and rich traditional flavour.
ingredients: 1 kg beef shank, cut into large pieces
½ cup cooking oil or ⅓ cup oil plus 1 tbsp ghee
3 tbsp nihari masala, or to taste
Fresh ginger, coriander, green chillies and lemon, for serving
method: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook until deep golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and beef. Sauté for about 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the meat changes colour and begins to brown.
Lower the heat, add the nihari masala and salt, and stir for about 30 seconds so the spices bloom without burning.

Pour in 7 cups hot water and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for about 4–6 hours, or until the beef shank is very tender. Add a little more hot water during cooking only if needed.
Take about 1 cup of nihari liquid from the pot and let it cool slightly. Whisk it gradually into the atta to make a smooth, lump-free slurry; do not add dry flour directly to the pot.
Slowly stir the slurry back into the nihari. Simmer gently for another 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the gravy is smooth and lightly thickened. Add hot water if it becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust salt. Garnish with julienned ginger, coriander and green chillies, and serve hot with lemon and naan.
tips: Make the flour slurry with nihari liquid rather than plain water so the gravy keeps its flavour.
Beef shank needs a long, gentle simmer; cook until it breaks easily when pressed.
After adding the atta slurry, simmer long enough for the raw flour taste to disappear.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Reheat until the meat and gravy are piping hot throughout.
serving: Serve hot with naan or sheermal, lemon wedges, fresh ginger, coriander and green chillies.
